definition: The two structures touch or are separated only by a plane of tissue. Symmetric, and therefore stored once: A adjacent to B is the same claim as B adjacent to A.
The subject lies in front of the object in standard anatomical position.
The subject is attached to the object: a tendon to a bone, a ligament to a capsule. FMA attaches_to.
The subject arises from the object in an arterial, ductal or nervous tree. Transitive: a branch of a branch is downstream of the trunk.

A part that is WHAT THE WHOLE IS MADE OF: renal cortex, gastric mucosa, myocardium. FMA constitutional_part_of. If you would name it as a tissue or a layer rather than as a place, this is the predicate.
The two structures are one anatomical continuity with a named transition. The proposition has one canonical symmetric identity; both original source-oriented relationship rows may be retained.
The subject empties its contents into the object.

The subject reaches the object only through intermediate vessels: the coeliac trunk indirectly supplies the spleen, and the splenic artery supplies it. Never an answer to "which vessel supplies this territory" — that question wants the direct supplier, and answering it with the trunk is wrong.

The subject is a kind of the object. Definitional rather than structural. In this snapshot every IS_A edge comes from FMA; some point at FMA grouping classes named "Branch of …" or "Tributary of …", which are not kinds (see README, Known limitations).
The subject lies closer to the midline than the object.

A part carved out by WHERE it is: fundus of the stomach, upper pole of the kidney, segment IV of the liver. FMA regional_part_of. If the part is named by its position or by a surgical/imaging landmark, this is the predicate.
The subject lies above the object in standard anatomical position. Proposed from measured segmentations across many subjects, never from one: a relation true in 54 per cent of people is not anatomy.

The subject provides arterial supply or innervation to the object. Read by "which vessel supplies this territory" cards, the question form behind every infarct pattern. In this snapshot every SUPPLIES edge is arterial supply; innervation is not included.

Membership of a body system, by WHAT IT DOES: the liver in the digestive system, the kidney in the urinary system. FMA systemic_part_of. The edge that makes an anatomy walk follow the body rather than the taxonomy — and the one a student is taught first.
The subject drains into the object in a venous or lymphatic tree.
